hints: Look at the two vertical arrows to the bottom of the U-tube: P is $10.0 \text{ cm}$ above the base and Q is $6.0 \text{ cm}$ above the base, so find the vertical separation of P above Q.
Pressure due to a liquid depends only on vertical height difference: $\Delta p = \rho g \Delta h$ with $\rho = 2000 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$.
Convert the separation from cm to m before multiplying by $\rho$ and $g = 9.81 \text{ m s}^{-2}$, then compare with the values in $\text{Pa}$.
walkthrough: Identify the levels from the diagram: P is at the top surface on the left, $10.0 \text{ cm}$ above the bottom datum, while Q is marked lower down on the right, $6.0 \text{ cm}$ above the same datum.
The pressure difference due to the liquid depends on the vertical distance between the two levels, so $\Delta h = 10.0 \text{ cm} - 6.0 \text{ cm} = 4.0 \text{ cm} = 0.040 \text{ m}$.
State the hydrostatic pressure rule: $\Delta p = \rho g \Delta h$, where $\rho = 2000 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$ and $g = 9.81 \text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Calculate the intermediate product: $9.81 \times 0.040 = 0.3924$, then $2000 \times 0.3924 \approx 785 \text{ Pa}$, which rounds to $780 \text{ Pa}$ with the given data.

options.A: Pressure difference is $\rho g \Delta h$ with $\Delta h = 0.040 \text{ m}$, giving about $780 \text{ Pa}$.
options.B: This uses only the $6.0 \text{ cm}$ height of Q above the base, not the vertical separation between P and Q.
options.C: This is larger than $\rho g$ times the $4.0 \text{ cm}$ separation between P and Q.
options.D: This uses the full $10.0 \text{ cm}$ depth of P, not the difference in level $10.0 \text{ cm} - 6.0 \text{ cm}$.
